Make BIND9 logging work

This ansible playbook configures BIND9 to activate logging in /var/log/bind/bind.log. For that to work AppArmor has to allow BIND access to that file. This change configures that access and informs AppArmor of the change so that it takes effect immediately.

feat: A playbook/role that changes imagemagick permissions to allow conversion of other formats to PDF

As a security feature, imagemagick defaults to refusing to produce PDF as an output format.
This role reverses that but should only be used on hosts that will not run imagemagick in response to web requests.

feat: Switch molecule testing of roles/home-common to use docker rather than vagrant

Debian distributions (10 and 9) required that locales be installed.
Ubuntu and Mint distributions failed to run timedatectl in a container because they could not access dbus. To fix that required a privileged container and access to the host's /run/dbus/system_bus_socket. This is done in molecule.yml. Then it transpired that the ansible timezone module needs /usr/shar/zoneinfo to be present and populated to verify the selected timezone (verified by reading the source code from https://galaxy.ansible.com/community/general). So install tzdata to ensure that these files are present.

Add molecule testing to the php role.

Different releases of different distributions often need different specific versions of PHP.
So aim to provide a distro-sepcific file (e.g. vars/Debian.yml) but allow for a release-specific version where necessary (e.g. vars/Debian-8.yml).

Also note that ansible_lsb is empty on CentOS, so provide a default string (that matches no YAML file) to avoid the CentOS test failing.
